name: Cookie prefix requirements not met
description:
The response sets a cookie whose name begins with __Host- or __Secure- (browsers match these prefixes case-insensitively) without the attributes the prefix requires. A __Secure- cookie must carry Secure; a __Host- cookie must carry Secure and Path=/ and no Domain attribute. A browser that implements cookie prefixes ignores such a Set-Cookie header entirely, and so does one that receives a nameless cookie whose value starts with a prefix.

The prefixes exist so that a server reading a prefixed cookie can rely on how it was set: a __Host- cookie cannot have been set or overwritten by a sibling subdomain or over cleartext. A server that sets a prefixed cookie without its attributes is therefore built on an assumption that does not hold: either the cookie never reaches the browser, and the application runs without it (often falling back to a less protected cookie), or a browser that does not enforce prefixes stores it without the protection the name promises.

This row is burpsy's own: Burp's catalogue has no row for cookie name prefixes. It is classified under CWE-693 (protection mechanism failure).
remediation: Set the attributes the prefix requires on every Set-Cookie header that uses it: Secure for __Secure-; Secure; Path=/ and no Domain for __Host-. Set prefixed cookies only over HTTPS. If the cookie must be shared with subdomains, use __Secure- rather than __Host-, and review whether sharing is needed at all.
